features.title: RAG playground searches in a LanceDB vector database, numpy as fallback
features.user_visible_behavior: `uv run rag-playground` searches a LanceDB table by default; `RAG_STORE=numpy` searches the same vectors in numpy. The startup line names the store. Both return the same chunks.
verification: Run ./init.sh.
Run the playground with RAG_STORE=lancedb and RAG_STORE=numpy and check the same sections are retrieved.
evidence: 2026-11-10: ./init.sh exit 0, pytest 110 passed (4 new, including a lancedb-vs-numpy order test).
2026-11-10: real index, 657 rows. Same top-5 chunks from both stores on 8 of 8 real questions, and on 200 of 200 chunk vectors used as queries. Table build 15 ms, search 8 ms.
features.notes: lancedb 0.41.0 on Python 3.14. No ANN index is created, so the search is exact. Not built: metadata filter by chapter (the table has a `section` column ready), hybrid keyword search, incremental adds.

features.title: RAG playground: hybrid (keyword + vector) search
features.user_visible_behavior: `uv run rag-playground --hybrid` (also with --agentic) searches by keyword (BM25) as well as by vector and merges the two lists. The startup line says 'hybrid search' or 'vector search'. Without the flag nothing changes.
verification: Run ./init.sh.
Run `uv run rag-playground --hybrid` against the real document and compare the retrieved chapters with a run without the flag on questions about rare names.
evidence: 2026-11-11: ./init.sh exit 0, pytest 112 passed (2 new: hybrid finds an exact name that vector search ranks last; hybrid with the numpy store raises).

2026-11-11: real index, 657 chunks. 14 questions 'Who or what is <name>?' for names found in 1 or 2 chunks: name in the top 5 for 11/14 with vector search and 14/14 with hybrid; chunks containing the name retrieved 14/18 and 18/18. Top result unchanged on 5 common questions. About 16 ms per search either way. Keyword index build is included in the ~50 ms table load.
2026-11-11: `uv run rag-playground --hybrid` answered 'Who is Imogene?' from Chapter 8; `RAG_STORE=numpy ... --hybrid` exits with a clear ValueError.
features.notes: LanceDB native FTS index on the `text` column with default settings, merged by LanceDB's default reciprocal rank fusion. Opt-in, because there is no eval set yet to show it is better overall: the measurement only checks that the name appears in a retrieved chunk, not that the answer is right. Not built: reranking, query rewriting, the eval set.

features.title: RAG playground: knowledge graph lookup tool for agentic mode
features.user_visible_behavior: `uv run rag-playground --agentic --graph` builds a knowledge graph of the campaign on first use (a local chat model reads every chunk once and writes down the relations between named things), saves it next to the index, and gives the model a campaign_relations tool to look a name up. An interrupted build continues where it stopped.
verification: Run ./init.sh.
Run `uv run rag-playground --agentic --graph` against the real document: check the build finishes, a second start skips it, and a question about connections makes the model call campaign_relations.
evidence: 2026-11-11: ./init.sh exit 0, pytest 118 passed (6 new: extraction, cache reuse, resume after interruption, name lookup, tool wiring, result cap).

2026-11-11: model trial on 3 real chunks. gemma4:e4b failed on 2 of 3. qwen3.8:27b worked at 36-52 s a chunk. qwen3.6:35b-a3b with thinking off: about 3 s a chunk and cleaner relations, so it is the default (RAG_GRAPH_MODEL).
2026-11-11: real build with qwen3.6:35b-a3b: 657 chunks in 118.3 min, 1,251 relations, 619 distinct names, 23 chunks skipped (unusable model output). A second start skipped the build.

2026-11-11: real run, `--agentic --graph`, gemma4:e4b: 'How are Cevan and Vecna connected?' called campaign_relations twice (101 and 33 relations) and answered that they are the same entity, citing chapters 24, 25, 29, 32, 38. 'Who is connected to the city of Kallista?' called it once (20 relations). With qwen3.6:35b-a3b and --hybrid the model called campaign_relations and then search_campaign on both questions.

2026-11-11: comparison without --graph, gemma4:e4b, same two questions: both answered; the Kallista answer lacked the governor (High King Thalion Arannis), Ryn and the Sable Enclave, which the graph run included.
features.notes: Small version on purpose: triples in a JSON file, lookup by substring on the name, no graph database, no clusters or summaries. Known limits: two spellings of a name stay two entities; relations carry the section they came from but no other notion of time. Seen in the real graph: aliases split one character over several names (Cevan, Lord Cevan, Vecna, Vecna the Undying), and some relations are wrong (e.g. 'Tiamat | was slain by | the narrator' from a world-building section). Answers were not fact-checked by someone who knows the campaign. The 23 skipped chunks are not retried.

features.title: RAG playground: knowledge graph quality (quoted evidence, names only, aliases)
features.user_visible_behavior: The graph build keeps a relation only when its chunk contains the sentence the model quotes for it and both names, and never a narrator in text without a first person. A model-drafted, hand-editable alias file (data/rag/<name>.aliases.json) makes campaign_relations return the relations of every name of the same character, and the tool shows the quoted sentence with each relation.
verification: Run ./init.sh.
Rebuild the graph on the real document (about two hours) and record relations kept and dropped.
Judge a random sample of 50 relations against their source sentences and compare with the old graph's sample.
Review the drafted alias file, then ask a question under one alias (Cevan) and check relations of the other (Vecna) come back.
evidence: 2026-11-11: ./init.sh exit 0, pytest 121 passed (3 new: the support check, alias draft and file, lookup across aliases).

2026-11-11: old graph, before the change. 104 of 1,251 relations name an end that is in no chunk of their section; 319 of 1,251 have an end with no capital letter ('cloak', 'the tavern'). In a random sample of 49 judged by Claude against the source sentences: 18 clearly stated relations between named things, 8 borderline, 23 junk or wrong.

2026-11-11: trial of the new extraction on 10 real chunks (before the capital-letter rule): 31 relations kept, 6 dropped; the made-up 'Tiamat was slain by' relation was dropped. Relations whose quote does not mean what the relation says still pass ('Roger | lives in | Daerin's home').

2026-11-11: alias draft on the old graph's 619 names, qwen3.6:35b-a3b, thinking off: 24 groups in 138 s. Right: Lord Cevan = Vecna = Cevan; the narrator = Ryn; Queen Sehara = Sehara; spelling variants. Doubtful: 'Rayl' in the Cevan group, 'Rosghonelian' in the Chiara group, 'Lou' with the narrator.
2026-11-11: NOT DONE: the real rebuild. It was started, then stopped at 13 of 657 chunks and put on hold at the user's request.
features.notes: Until the rebuild runs, --graph has no graph: the cache key now includes the prompt, so the old graph is not loaded and the next --graph start begins the two-hour build. The old graph is kept as data/rag/setting-the-darkness-ablaze.graph-v1.json (git-ignored). The checks are deterministic and do not judge meaning; a second model pass that checks each relation was not built.

features.title: RAG playground: grep tool for agentic mode (--grep)
features.user_visible_behavior: `uv run rag-playground --agentic --grep` gives the model a grep_campaign tool next to search_campaign: a case-insensitive regular expression over every paragraph, no index. Each hit is the section title plus up to 200 characters either side of the first match; at most 30 hits, then '... and N more'. An invalid pattern returns an error message the model can fix. --grep without --agentic is refused.
verification: Run ./init.sh.
Run the tool on the real document and check result size and speed.
Ask one real question with --agentic --grep.
evidence: 2026-11-17: ./init.sh exit 0 (see claude-progress.md session log); 4 new tests (matching and errors, snippet window, cap, agent calls the tool).

2026-11-17: real document, 657 chunks: 4 to 9 ms per grep. First version returned whole paragraphs: 8,243 words for 'Vecna|Cevan'. With 200-character snippets: 2,134 words ('Vecna|Cevan', 123 hits capped at 30) and 1,663 ('silver').

2026-11-17: gemma4:e2b, 'Which chapters mention the Silver Hand, and what is it?': search_campaign returned 5 story chapters and missed the Factions of Aeloria section; grep_campaign('Silver Hand') found its 2 paragraphs and the answer came from them.
features.notes: Added next to search_campaign, not instead of it, so the model picks. Not measured: the 14 name questions used for --hybrid, or grep alone versus hybrid. Only the first match per paragraph is shown.

verification: Run ./init.sh.
Run uv run rag-eval on the real document and record the table.
evidence: 2026-11-17: ./init.sh exit 0; new test for score/by_grep/by_index on a fake index.

features.notes: The user has not reviewed the questions yet. Too easy to rank modes: 1 question apart is noise. It measures retrieval only (any answering section in the results), not rank or answer quality. Grep gets a hand-written pattern, an upper bound on what a model would write. Grep returns up to 30 snippets, vector/hybrid 5 chunks, so compare words too.

features.title: Token usage per turn
features.user_visible_behavior: After every answer, gezellig-ai and rag-playground --agentic print the turn's requests and input/output tokens plus the conversation total; two-step RAG prints its one request; the Streamlit Assistant shows the turn's tokens in the 'Thought for' label. One helper, ai_playground.agent.token_usage(messages), sums the usage each model response carries, so it keeps no state and is safe for the agent shared between Streamlit sessions.

features.title: Campaign search tools as an MCP server (rag-mcp)
features.user_visible_behavior: `uv run rag-mcp [--hybrid]` serves search_campaign and grep_campaign over MCP (stdio), marked read-only, with server instructions describing the campaign. Any MCP client can start it, e.g. `claude mcp add campaign -- uv run --project <repo> rag-mcp --hybrid`. The tools' log lines go to stderr because stdout carries the protocol.
verification: Run ./init.sh.
Start the server over stdio from a real MCP client, list tools, call one, and let an agent use it.
evidence: 2026-11-17: ./init.sh exit 0; new test lists both tools with their schemas and read-only flag, calls grep_campaign, and checks nothing reached stdout.

2026-11-17: pydantic-ai MCPToolset over StdioTransport('uv run rag-mcp --hybrid') on the real document: tools listed; grep_campaign('Thavaadi') returned Chapter 28; a pydantic-ai agent on the local default model with only that toolset called search_campaign and answered 'Remorhaz' to the ice-worm question (correct, Chapter 42).
features.notes: Added pydantic-ai-slim[mcp] (mcp 2.3, fastmcp). mcp 2.x renamed FastMCP to MCPServer; pydantic-ai's client is MCPToolset. Not tried from Claude Code itself: that needs `claude mcp add`, which changes the user's Claude config. No graph tool on the server yet (the graph is not rebuilt).
